description:
The Relation Grid primitive (RFC 0050 · Episode 2). The root principle
        is the whole contract: the grid captures intents and arranges cells;
        it holds, fetches, pushes and writes NO VALUE. A relation is
        identities, columns and a CELL MANAGER (cellFor) — the grid asks for a
        cell once per identity and places it; the domain owns the cell for its
        whole life and updates it directly.

        What is here: arrangement over an immutable root relation; a cursor
        that is an identity with a position as its fallback; the shallow/deep
        discipline (single click and arrows are the grid's; Enter or a
        double-click hands the cell control until it releases); column widths
        held by identity, applied by position, in place. What is not: sort,
        filter, selection ranges — the relation's and later rounds'.

        Value-freedom is enforced mechanically — a test scans every grid
        module for the value verbs and fails the build on the first one. The
        JS has no runtime dependency on homing; the Java side is packaging.
